# CPC to practice-area sector mapping

Target firm: **Foley & Lardner LLP** · CPC edition **2026.08**

Every code below was validated against the official CPC scheme and its title attached from the published title list. The *why* column is analyst judgment and is the part worth arguing with.

| | |
|---|---|
| CPC symbols in scheme | 254,314 |
| CPC subclasses in scheme | 681 |
| Subclasses mapped to a sector | 53 |
| Subclass coverage | 7.78% |

Low coverage is expected and correct: four practice areas should not span all of human invention.

## Cross-cutting decisions

### `overlap-allowed`

**Decision.** A patent may map to more than one sector. It is not forced into exactly one.

**Why.** A machine-learning model for reading radiology images is genuinely relevant to both the Health Care and Innovative Technology teams. Forcing an exclusive assignment would encode a false choice and would hide exactly the companies that sit at a lucrative intersection.

**Consequence.** Sector patent counts MUST NOT be summed to a firm-wide total; the sum double-counts. Each sector is reported independently, and the overlap rate is published alongside so a reader can see how much double-assignment occurs.

### `y-section-excluded`

**Decision.** CPC section Y (Y02, Y04S, Y10) is excluded from all sectors.

**Why.** Y is a tagging overlay applied on top of a patent's real classification, not a classification in its own right. A solar inverter patent already carries H02S or H02J; adding its Y02E tag would count the same invention twice within the same sector and inflate Energy relative to every other sector.

**Consequence.** Energy counts are lower than a Y02E-based query would produce. This is deliberate and is the more defensible number.

### `subclass-default`

**Decision.** Map at CPC subclass level by default; drop to main group only where a subclass spans genuinely different industries.

**Why.** Group-level mapping (thousands of codes) is unmaintainable by one analyst and creates an illusion of precision the underlying judgment does not support. Subclass level is coarse enough to defend line by line in an interview.

**Consequence.** Some irrelevant patents are swept in at the edges of each subclass. The resulting noise is a known limitation, reported rather than hidden.

### `no-revenue-proxy`

**Decision.** Sector assignment reflects the technology, not the company's industry.

**Why.** A conglomerate that patents in A61B is doing medical device work regardless of how its revenue is classified by SIC or NAICS. The signal this project scores is patent activity, so the sector must be read off the patent.

**Consequence.** A company may appear in a sector that its investor-relations material would not claim. That is a feature for business development, but it means sector labels here are not company classifications and must not be presented as such.

## Sectors

### Energy

Generation, storage, conversion, and distribution of power, plus extraction of the fuels that feed it. Patent activity here tracks capital deployment into new energy assets, which reliably precedes transactional and regulatory legal work.

Kept here as a deliberate record of the change, because any mapping inherited from older work will still name it and will silently match nothing.

## Cross-sector overlap

These prefixes are claimed by more than one sector. This is intended (see `overlap-allowed`) and is why sector counts must never be summed.

- `H10P` → innovative_technology, manufacturing

## Known limitations

- Subclass-level mapping sweeps in edge patents that a specialist would exclude. No claim is made that every patent counted in a sector is relevant to that practice; the claim is that the ranking between companies is stable under that noise, which the scoring phase must test rather than assume.
- The four sectors do not partition CPC. Large areas -- textiles, construction, agriculture, food -- map to no sector and are simply out of scope for this firm. Coverage against the full scheme is reported by the build script.
- CPC is revised quarterly and codes are retired. The first draft of this mapping used H01L for semiconductors and H01L31/00 for photovoltaics; both were retired in the 2023 reorganisation into the H10 series and match nothing in edition 2026.08. Validation against the published scheme caught it. Any sector map that is written once and never re-validated will decay the same way, silently, because a retired code produces zero matches rather than an error.
- The mapping reflects one analyst's reading of one firm's published industry teams. It is a starting point for a conversation with the practice group, not a finished taxonomy, and it carries no endorsement from the firm.
